problem: Traditional 3D scene graphs rely on multi-level semantic hierarchies (room/region nodes) that risk semantic discrepancies between high-level nodes and the objects they contain, and they separate semantic context from way-topology, disconnecting scene understanding from actionable navigation.
motivation: Robots need a robust, sparse environment representation for zero-shot object navigation that links what is seen to where to go. Merging context and traversable topology in one structure is meant to make the semantics continuous and directly usable for planning, with both visual (image) and textual queries.
key_idea: Build a two-layer hierarchical 3D scene graph, an object layer plus a 'conway' layer (contextual information + way topology), in which topological waypoints carry multi-modal context so scene interpretation and navigation are unified.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The paper's claim is that attaching multi-modal context to waypoint nodes, rather than to abstract room/region nodes, avoids high-level/object semantic mismatch and aligns the representation with navigation.
method: Object layer: nodes for detected objects in the 3D scene graph.
Conway layer: waypoint-topology nodes that also store multi-modal contextual information (contextual info + way topology), replacing multi-level semantic hierarchies.
Navigation-centric alignment: observations are aligned with navigation-centric perspectives to link scene understanding with task execution.
Query interface: supports both visual (image goal) and textual (language) queries for zero-shot object navigation.

setting.backbone: not specified in abstract (zero-shot, likely foundation-model-based perception/language)
